The Criteria API has no cast expression: a predicate compares a path against a literal or another path. The reference's one string() form is over a BOOLEAN column, whose CEL text is exactly "true" or "false" and is compared in Java; over any other column type string() is refused in the leaf operand, because a number's text form is what the dialects render on their own terms and nothing in the Criteria API reproduces CEL's

Arithmetic comparison requires numeric o: The comparison is a_optional_string against a concatenation of a constant with the primary key. The reference lowers CEL's `+` as arithmetic, which requires numeric operands; CEL's string overload has no arithmetic meaning and is refused rather than rendered as a numeric addition

The same arithmetic-only lowering of `+`, reached with both operands columns instead of one being a constant. The reference refuses every string `+`, so it needs no type information to reject the two-column form
arithmetic composed on a division whose: CEL carries a NaN or signed infinity through the arithmetic composed on top of a division, and SQL has no value that does — the NULLIF divide-by-zero guard turns the whole sum into NULL. The reference's non-finite rewrite only reaches a division that IS the comparison operand, so a division nested inside further arithmetic fails closed rather than emitting the under-granting filter
Same nested-division limitation as cr-div-then-add. This is the arm that proves it matters: `NaN != 2.0` is TRUE and the PDP allows the zero row, while `NULL + 1 <> 2` is UNKNOWN and drops it
mod is not supported in comparisons: CEL: CEL `%` is integer-only while attribute values are doubles, so a satisfiable policy has to cast with int() first — and int() has no faithful SQL lowering, CAST rounding where CEL truncates toward zero. The same limitation refuses cast-int-double
Direct comparison of map(...) to a value: map() translates only as the collection operand of hasIntersection, where the projection becomes the inner select of an EXISTS. Comparing the ordered projection itself to a literal list has no Criteria form
hierarchy delimiter must be a non-empty: Cerbos splits a path on an empty delimiter into one segment per character, so the relation is a strict string-prefix test; the reference lowers descendentOf as `LIKE prefix + delimiter + '%'`, which with an empty delimiter also matches the path itself (a2, never its own descendant). The empty delimiter is refused when the hierarchy operand is resolved, before that LIKE is built
